arxiv-2105-00627.title: Improving Community Detection Performance in Heterogeneous Music Network by Learning Edge-type Usefulness Distribution
arxiv-2105-00627.creator: Zheng Gao, Chun Guo, Shutian Ma, Xiaozhong Liu
arxiv-2105-00627.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Zheng Gao, Chun Guo, Shutian Ma, Xiaozhong Liu. With music becoming an essential part of daily life, there is an urgent need to develop recommendation systems to assist people targeting better songs with fewer efforts. As the interactions between users and songs naturally construct a complex network, community detection approaches can be applied to reveal users’ potential interests on songs by grouping relevant users & songs to the same community.

arxiv-2112-11306.title: Hodge classes of type ( 2 , 2 ) (2,2) on Hilbert squares of projective K3 surfaces
arxiv-2112-11306.creator: Simone Novario
arxiv-2112-11306.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Simone Novario. We give a basis for the vector space generated by rational Hodge classes of type ( 2 , 2 ) (2,2) on the Hilbert square of a projective K3 surface general in its rank, which is a subspace of the singular cohomology ring with rational coefficients: we use Nakajima operators and an algebraic model developed by Lehn and Sorger as main tools.

arxiv-2311-00275.title: Stochastic viability in an island model with partial dispersal : Approximation by a diffusion process in the limit of a large number of islands
arxiv-2311-00275.creator: Dhaker Kroumi, Sabin Lessard
arxiv-2311-00275.description: Abstract Abstract In this paper, we study a finite population undergoing discrete, nonoverlapping generations, that is structured into D demes, each containing N individuals of two possible types, A and B , whose viability coefficients, s_{A} and s_{B} , respectively, vary randomly from one generation to the next.

arxiv-2404-12686.title: The M onument Experiment: Ordinary Muon Capture studies for 0 ​ ν ​ β ​ β 0\nu\beta\beta decay
arxiv-2404-12686.creator: G. R. Araujo addr1, D. Bajpai addr2, L. Baudis addr1, V. Belov addr4, addr5, E. Bossio addr5, addr6, e2, T.E. Cocolios addr7, H. Ejiri addr8, M. Fomina addr4, K. Gusev addr4, addr5, I.H. Hashim addr9, M. Heines addr7, S. Kazartsev addr4, A. Knecht addr10, E. Mondragón addr5, e1, Z.W. Ng addr9, I. Os
arxiv-2404-12686.description: Abstract The M onument experiment measures ordinary muon capture (OMC) on isotopes relevant for neutrinoless double-beta ( 0 ​ ν ​ β ​ β 0\nu\beta\beta ) decay and nuclear astrophysics. OMC is a particularly attractive tool for improving the theoretical description of 0 ​ ν ​ β ​ β 0\nu\beta\beta decay.

arxiv-2412-16874.title: A Multi-modal Approach to Dysarthria Detection and Severity Assessment Using Speech and Text Information
arxiv-2412-16874.creator: 1 st Anuprabha M, 2 nd Krishna Gurugubelli, 3 rd Kesavaraj.v, 4 th Anil Kumar Vuppala, Anuprabha M 1 , Krishna Gurugubelli 2 , Kesavaraj V 1 , Anil Kumar Vuppala 1
arxiv-2412-16874.description: Abstract Automatic detection and severity assessment of dysarthria are crucial for delivering targeted therapeutic interventions to patients. While most existing research focuses primarily on speech modality, this study introduces a novel approach that leverages both speech and text modalities. By employing cross-attention mechanism, our method learns the acoustic and linguistic similarities between speech and text representations.

pmc-10656442.title: Mock community experiments can inform on the reliability of eDNA metabarcoding data: a case study on marine phytoplankton
pmc-10656442.creator: Nadia Marinchel, Alexis Marchesini, Davide Nardi, Matteo Girardi, Silvia Casabianca, Cristiano Vernesi, Antonella Penna
pmc-10656442.description: Environmental DNA metabarcoding is increasingly implemented in biodiversity monitoring, including phytoplankton studies. Using 21 mock communities composed of seven unicellular diatom and dinoflagellate algae, assembled with different composition and abundance by controlling the number of cells, we tested the accuracy of an eDNA metabarcoding protocol in reconstructing patterns of alpha and beta diversity.

pmc-10736784.title: ONLINE COGNITIVE MONITORING IN A SIMULATED ANTI-AMYLOID TRIAL: ADHERENCE AND COGNITIVE CHANGE
pmc-10736784.creator: Jeffrey Kaye, Nora Mattek, Jennifer Marcoe, Amanda Mar, Yanan Shang, Aimee Pierce, Kevin Duff, Adriana Hughes
pmc-10736784.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). Remote assessment of cognitive function is increasingly of interest for monitoring cognitive decline. Additional advantages of remote monitoring are more frequent assessments and the examination of change over time, which may yield more sensitive indicators of cognitive status. This concept was tested in DETECT-AD (Digital Evaluations and Technologies Enabling Clinical Translation for Alzheimer’s Disease), an ongoing simulated anti-amyloid trial using digital biomarkers as outcome measures.

pmc-11360049.title: Characterization of the SARS-CoV-2 Genome 3′-Untranslated Region Interactions with Host MicroRNAs
pmc-11360049.creator: Caleb
pmc-11360049.description: The 2019 pandemic, caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2), has marked the spread of a novel human coronavirus. SARS-CoV-2 has exhibited increased disease severity and immune evasion across its variants, and the molecular mechanisms behind these phenomena remain largely unknown.

pmc-11614579.title: Biomarkers Reflecting the Severity of Bronchial Asthma in Children
pmc-11614579.creator: Peter Kunc, Michal Pokusa, Dominika Hajduchova, Jaroslav Fabry, Marek Samec, Martina Neuschlova, Renata Pecova
pmc-11614579.description: BackgroundBronchial asthma, the most prevalent chronic inflammatory airway disease in children, exhibits a concerning rise in both incidence and prevalence. Asthma biomarkers hold promise for stratifying patients into distinct clinical phenotypes, paving the way for targeted and personalized treatment approaches.

pmc-11716633.title: Identification of cross‐diagnostic protein signatures and subtypes of neurodegenerative diseases using multi‐task deep learning on the UK Biobank proteomics dataset
pmc-11716633.creator: Tomasz Gargas, Liping Hou, Tomasz Wrzesinski, Konrad Wojtowicz, Marta Kowalska, Malgorzata Kamuda, Tomasz Jetka, Christopher D Whelan, Bart Smets
pmc-11716633.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundNeurodegenerative diseases are a heterogeneous group of illnesses. Differences across patients exist in the underlying biological drivers of disease. Furthermore, cross‐diagnostic disease mechanisms exist, and different pathologies often co‐occur in the brain. Clinical symptoms fail to capture this heterogeneity. Molecular biomarker‐driven approaches are needed to improve patient identification & stratification with the aim of moving towards more targeted patient treatment strategies.MethodThe UK Biobank Pharma Proteomics Project has generated a proteomics dataset of unprecedented size.

pmc-12422030.title: Effects of Interventions to Improve Access to Financial Services for Micro, Small, and Medium‐Sized Enterprises in Low‐ and Middle‐Income Countries: An Evidence and Gap Map
pmc-12422030.creator: Nina Ashley O Dela Cruz, Alyssa Cyrielle B Villanueva, Lovely Tolin, Sabrina Disse, Robert Lensink, Howard White
pmc-12422030.description: Micro, small, and medium‐sized enterprises (MSMEs) account for most firms in most economies, particularly in developing nations, and are key contributors to job creation and global economic development. However, the most significant impediment to MSME development in low‐ and middle‐income countries is a lack of access to both investment and working capital financing.

pmc-13109897.creator: Yong Chen, Hans J. Kaper, Theo van Kooten, Prashant Kumar Sharma

pmc-13331148.title: Effect of modified anterior approach for ultrasound-guided superior laryngeal nerve block on sore throat after tonsillectomy in adults: study protocol for a double-blind randomised controlled trial
pmc-13331148.creator: Hong Li, Ruihao Zhou, Yusi Hua, Jianqiao Zheng, Guo Chen, Tao Zhu
pmc-13331148.description: IntroductionPostoperative sore throat (POST), a common complication following tonsillectomy, significantly impairs patient recovery through persistent pain and dysphagia. The internal branch of superior laryngeal nerve block (iSLNB) can effectively alleviate POST. Specifically, the ultrasound (US)-guided modified anterior approach for iSLNB offers anatomical precision and reduced invasiveness compared with traditional approaches.

pmc-13572598.title: Virtual reality for rehabilitation and engagement in pediatric intensive care: a systematic review of feasibility, safety and outcomes
pmc-13572598.creator: Insu Choi, Hwa Jin Cho, Kibum Kim, Sunyong Yoo, Min-Keun Song
pmc-13572598.description: Children admitted to pediatric intensive care units (PICUs) are at risk of acquired weakness, delirium, and long-term functional and neurocognitive morbidity. Although early rehabilitation is recommended to mitigate these adverse outcomes, its delivery remains challenging. Virtual reality (VR) has been proposed as a means of enhancing engagement in rehabilitation in this setting.
